shortLabel: The departure test has an instrument and has never been run

sources.alignmentNote: The facet panel is the evidence that the burial arm exists and is populated; the counts are an upper bound because the variants engine is loose and the rows must be read.
sources.locator: sid=102 parent search, fatherfirstname=john and fatherlastname=gurney both variant-expanded, collection=parish+baptisms, sourcecountry=great+britain, yearofbirth=1630&yearofbirth_offset=5, 28 July 2026: facet panel reports Parish Baptisms 108, Parish Burials 76, Parish Marriages 13, Wills & Probate 0; year=1630&year_offset=10 returns 0 while rendering a chip

statement: The natural inversion of the search - which John Gurney household's records stop between 1635 and 1641 without a burial or probate for the head - has been treated as something to do parish by parish. It is not. The parent-name search runs over burials as well as baptisms: a father-John-Gurney sweep for 1625-1635 reports, in one facet panel, 108 parish baptisms, 76 parish burials and 13 parish marriages. Switching the collection to parish burials therefore asks in a single query which children of a John Gurney were buried in England, and the households appearing in the baptism arm but not the burial arm are exactly the departure-shaped gaps. Two mechanics have to be right first: the year parameter in this mode must be the birth-year form, because the plain year parameter renders a filter chip and then returns a silent zero; and the pool excludes some county sets, so the burial arm needs pairing with county-set runs exactly as the baptism arm does. This is the highest-value single query left on the child inventory and it has never been executed - which is the wider point the method was written for: this work has repeatedly gained more from establishing that an instrument said what it appeared to say than from running more searches.

unit.title: Identity — method for a complete child inventory
